description:
Retrieve the list of chats that the user is part of. This method supports federation. When a user ID is provided, the calling application must belong to the same tenant that the user belongs to.

TIP: Lists all Teams chats a specific user is a member of (1:1, group, meeting chats). Each chat has id, topic (for group/meeting chats; null for 1:1), chatType (oneOnOne | group | meeting), createdDateTime, lastUpdatedDateTime, webUrl, viewpoint. Use as the entry point for security investigations on a specific user — list their chats, then drill into messages with list-chat-messages. IMPORTANT: this is admin-level surveillance access — only call with documented investigative purpose (security incident, legal hold pending eDiscovery case, HR investigation with sign-off). For formal legal discovery (subpoena response, litigation), prefer the eDiscovery v3 workflow (create-ediscovery-case → custodian → search → reviewSet → export) which provides chain-of-custody and is the Microsoft-recommended pattern for court-admissible exports. Supports $filter, $top, $skip, $expand=lastMessagePreview, $orderby. BILLING: as of 2025-08-25 the Teams Export APIs (including Chat.Read.All / ChatMessage.Read.All in application mode) are NO LONGER METERED — no Azure subscription billing setup required. (Recordings and transcripts still use per-license model parameter — see docs/METERED_APIS.md.)
